book.old: <>클라라의 짧은 발판 기억나요? 그 줄에는 진짜 이름이 있어요: {A('B1', '덧줄')}. 덧줄은 {A('B2', '사다리의 발판')}이에요. 음이 나라 밖으로 나갈 때, 퀸즈랜드 위로는 새가 사는 하늘까지, 킹스랜드 아래로는 거북이 사는 바다까지 올라가고 내려가게 해 줘요.
book.new: <>클라라의 짧은 발판에는 진짜 이름이 있어요: {A('B1', '덧줄')}. 덧줄은 나라 밖으로 나가는 {A('B2', '사다리의 발판')}이에요. 퀸즈랜드 위로는 새의 하늘로, 킹스랜드 아래로는 거북의 바다로 가요.

book.old: <>Remember Clara's little ladder? It has a real name: a {A('B1', 'ledger line')}. Ledger lines are {A('B2', 'little ladders')} that let notes climb out of the lands: up from Queensland into the bird's sky, down from Kingsland into the turtle's sea.
book.new: <>Clara's little ladder has a real name: a {A('B1', 'ledger line')}. Ledger lines are {A('B2', 'little ladders')} out of the lands: up from Queensland into the bird's sky, down from Kingsland into the turtle's sea.

book.old: <>음이 오선 안에 들어가지 못할 만큼 높거나 낮으면, 그 음 하나만을 위해 짧은 줄을 그어요. 이게 덧줄이고, 클라라의 발판도 덧줄이에요. 줄-칸-줄-칸 무늬는 오선 밖에서도 그대로 이어져요. 덧줄은 음표보다 살짝 넓게, 오선과 같은 간격으로, 오선까지 빈틈없이, 음표에 필요한 만큼만 그어요. 칸에 있는 음 위에는 뚜껑처럼 한 줄 더 긋지 않아요.
book.new: <>오선보다 너무 높거나 낮은 음에는 그 음만을 위한 짧은 줄을 그어요: 덧줄. 클라라의 발판도 덧줄이에요. 무늬는 오선 밖에서도 이어져요: 줄, 칸, 줄, 칸. 덧줄은 음표보다 살짝 넓게, 오선과 같은 간격으로, 오선까지 빈틈없이 그어요. 한 줄도 더 긋지 않아요: 칸 음 위에는 뚜껑이 없어요.

book.old: <>When a note is too high or too low for the five lines, we draw a short line just for that note: a ledger line. Clara's ladder is one. The pattern carries on outside the staff: line, space, line, space. A ledger line is just a little wider than the note, the same distance apart as the staff lines, with no gaps back to the staff, and never one more than the note needs: a note in a space gets no lid on top.
book.new: <>A note too high or too low for the staff gets a short line of its own: a ledger line. Clara's ladder is one. The pattern goes on outside the staff: line, space, line, space. Draw it a little wider than the note, the same distance apart as the staff lines, with no gaps back to the staff. Never one too many: a note in a space gets no lid.

book.old: <>가운데 도를 쳐요. 그 음이 앉은 짧은 줄의 진짜 이름은 덧줄이에요.
book.new: <>가운데 도를 쳐요. 그 음이 앉은 짧은 줄이 덧줄이에요.

book.old: <>덧줄 위의 음을 하나 더 쳐요: 퀸즈랜드 위 발판의 A. 가운데 도와 A, 둘 다 덧줄 위에 있어요.
book.new: <>퀸즈랜드 위 발판의 A를 쳐요. 이 음도 덧줄 위에 있어요.

book.old: <>Play middle C. The short line it sits on has a real name: a ledger line.
book.new: <>Play middle C. The short line it sits on is a ledger line.

book.old: <>Play one more note on a ledger line: the A on the ladder above Queensland. Middle C and that A both sit on ledger lines.
book.new: <>Play the A on the ladder above Queensland. It sits on a ledger line too.

book.old: <>퀸즈랜드의 맨 윗줄 F에서 출발해요. 바로 위 칸은 {bkChapterNo('whole-staff')}챕터의 G. 그 위 1번 발판은 A, 그다음 칸은 B, 2번 발판은 C, {A('B3', 높은 도)}예요. 줄, 칸, 줄, 칸: 오선 안에서처럼 한 걸음에 한 글자씩. {A('B4', <>발판은 세 개까지: 3번 발판은 E.)}
book.new: <>퀸즈랜드 맨 윗줄 F에서 출발해요. 바로 위 칸은 {bkChapterNo('whole-staff')}챕터의 G. 1번 발판은 A, 다음 칸은 B, 2번 발판은 C, {A('B3', 높은 도)}예요. 오선 안에서처럼 한 걸음에 한 글자씩. {A('B4', <>발판은 세 개까지: 3번 발판은 E.)}

book.old: <>Start on Queensland's top line, F. Just above it, in the space, is Chapter {bkChapterNo('whole-staff')}'s G. Then ladder 1 carries A, the next space B, and ladder 2 carries C, {A('B3', high C)}. Line, space, line, space: one letter a step, just like inside the staff. {A('B4', <>We go as high as three ladders: ladder 3 is E.)}
book.new: <>Start on Queensland's top line, F. The space above is Chapter {bkChapterNo('whole-staff')}'s G. Ladder 1 is A, the next space B, and ladder 2 is C, {A('B3', high C)}. One letter a step, as inside the staff. {A('B4', <>We go as high as three ladders: ladder 3 is E.)}

book.old: <>킹스랜드의 맨 아랫줄 G에서 아래로 내려가요. 바로 아래 칸은 {bkChapterNo('whole-staff')}챕터의 F. 1번 발판은 E, 그다음 칸은 D, 2번 발판은 C, {A('B3', 낮은 도)}예요. 거북이 사는 바다까지 한 걸음에 한 글자씩, 거꾸로: G F E D C. {A('B4', <>3번 발판은 A.)}
book.new: <>킹스랜드 맨 아랫줄 G에서 내려가요. 바로 아래 칸은 {bkChapterNo('whole-staff')}챕터의 F. 1번 발판은 E, 다음 칸은 D, 2번 발판은 C, {A('B3', 낮은 도)}예요. 거북의 바다로 한 걸음에 한 글자씩, 거꾸로: G F E D C. {A('B4', <>3번 발판은 A.)}

book.old: <>Now climb down from Kingsland's bottom line, G. Just under it, in the space, is Chapter {bkChapterNo('whole-staff')}'s F. Ladder 1 carries E, the next space D, and ladder 2 carries C, {A('B3', low C)}, down in the turtle's sea. One letter a step, backwards: G F E D C. {A('B4', <>Ladder 3 is A.)}
book.new: <>Climb down from Kingsland's bottom line, G. The space below is Chapter {bkChapterNo('whole-staff')}'s F. Ladder 1 is E, the next space D, and ladder 2 is C, {A('B3', low C)}. One letter a step, backwards, into the turtle's sea: G F E D C. {A('B4', <>Ladder 3 is A.)}

book.old: <>{A('B6', <>두 나라 사이의 발판은 빌려 온 줄이에요. 퀸즈랜드 아래 2번 발판의 A는 킹스랜드의 맨 윗줄 A와 같은 건반이고, 킹스랜드 위 2번 발판의 E는 퀸즈랜드의 맨 아랫줄 E와 같은 건반이에요. 가운데 도는 어느 나라에서 봐도 발판 하나 위에 있어요. 같은 건반을 두 가지로 쓸 수 있어서, 두 손이 각자 자기 나라에 머물 수 있어요.)}
book.new: <>{A('B6', <>두 나라 사이의 발판은 빌려 온 줄이에요. 퀸즈랜드 아래 2번 발판의 A는 킹스랜드 맨 윗줄 A와 같은 건반이에요. 킹스랜드 위 2번 발판의 E는 퀸즈랜드 맨 아랫줄 E와 같은 건반이에요. 가운데 도는 어느 나라에서 봐도 발판 하나 위에 있어요. 같은 건반을 두 가지로 쓰니, 두 손이 각자 자기 나라에 머물러요.)}

book.old: <>{A('B6', <>The ladders between the lands are borrowed. The A on ladder 2 under Queensland is the same key as Kingsland's top line, A; the E on ladder 2 over Kingsland is the same key as Queensland's bottom line, E. Middle C sits on one ladder, seen from either land. The same key can be written two ways, so each hand can stay in its own land.)}
book.new: <>{A('B6', <>The ladders between the lands are borrowed. The A on ladder 2 under Queensland is the same key as Kingsland's top line, A. The E on ladder 2 over Kingsland is the same key as Queensland's bottom line, E. Middle C sits on one ladder, seen from either land. The same key, written two ways, lets each hand stay in its own land.)}

book.old: <>위 그림의 세 쌍을 쳐요: A, C, E, 각각 한 번은 오른손, 한 번은 왼손으로. 같은 소리예요!</>
book.new: <>세 쌍 A, C, E를 각각 오른손으로 한 번, 왼손으로 한 번 쳐요. 같은 소리예요!</>

book.old: <>Play the three pairs above: A, C and E, each once with the right hand, once with the left. The same sound!</>
book.new: <>Play the three pairs, A, C and E, each once with the right hand and once with the left. The same sound!</>

book.old: <>바다에서 하늘까지 C가 다섯 개, 한 옥타브씩 떨어져 있어요: {A('B3', 낮은 도)}, 낮은음자리표 도, 가운데 도, 높은음자리표 도, {A('B3', 높은 도)}. {bkChapterNo('whole-staff')}챕터처럼 클라라의 발판에서 접어 보면 C끼리 짝을 지어 만나요: 높은음자리표 도는 낮은음자리표 도에, 그리고 이제 높은 도는 낮은 도에, 발판 둘 위, 발판 둘 아래. 이 책의 덧줄 음은 모두 낮은 도, 가운데 도, 높은 도에서 한 걸음이나 건너뛰기면 닿아요.
book.new: <>바다에서 하늘까지 C 다섯 개가 한 옥타브씩 떨어져 있어요: {A('B3', 낮은 도)}, 낮은음자리표 도, 가운데 도, 높은음자리표 도, {A('B3', 높은 도)}. {bkChapterNo('whole-staff')}챕터처럼 클라라의 발판에서 접으면 짝끼리 만나요: 높은음자리표 도는 낮은음자리표 도와, 이제 높은 도는 낮은 도와, 발판 둘 위, 둘 아래. 이 책의 덧줄 음은 모두 낮은 도, 가운데 도, 높은 도에서 한 걸음이나 건너뛰기예요.

book.old: <>From the sea to the sky there are five Cs, an octave apart: {A('B3', low C)}, bass C, middle C, treble C and {A('B3', high C)}. Fold at Clara's ladder, like in Chapter {bkChapterNo('whole-staff')}, and they meet in pairs: treble C on bass C, and now high C on low C, two ladders up, two ladders down. Every ledger note in this book is a step or a skip from low C, middle C or high C.
book.new: <>Five Cs sit an octave apart, from the sea to the sky: {A('B3', low C)}, bass C, middle C, treble C and {A('B3', high C)}. Fold at Clara's ladder, as in Chapter {bkChapterNo('whole-staff')}, and they meet in pairs: treble C on bass C, now high C on low C, two ladders up, two down. Every ledger note in this book is a step or a skip from low C, middle C or high C.

book.old: <>접기 짝: 낮은 도와 높은 도를 두 손으로 같이, 그다음 낮은음자리표 도와 높은음자리표 도, 마지막에 두 엄지로 가운데 도, 두 손이 접는 선으로 모여요.
book.new: <>접기 짝: 낮은 도와 높은 도를 두 손으로 같이, 그다음 낮은음자리표 도와 높은음자리표 도, 마지막에 두 엄지로 가운데 도. 두 손이 접는 선에서 만나요.

guide.old: Notes don't stop at the edge of the staff. Short extra lines (ledger lines) are little ladders that let them climb out: up into the sky over the treble staff, down into the sea under the bass staff.
guide.new: Notes don't stop at the edge of the staff. Short ledger lines are little ladders out of it: up into the sky over the treble staff, down into the sea under the bass staff.

guide.old: When a note is too high or too low for the five lines, we draw a short line just for that note: a ledger line (also spelled leger). Middle C sits on one. In this book it is Clara's ladder. The pattern simply carries on outside the staff: line, space, line, space.
guide.new: A note too high or too low for the staff gets a short line of its own: a ledger line. Its other spelling is leger. Middle C sits on one, Clara's ladder in this book. The pattern goes on outside the staff: line, space, line, space.

guide.old: Drawing one neatly: a ledger line is a little wider than the note, the same distance apart as the staff lines, with no gaps back to the staff. And never one more than the note needs: a note in a space gets no lid on top.
guide.new: Draw it a little wider than the note, the same distance apart as the staff lines, with no gaps back to the staff. Never one too many: a note in a space gets no lid.

guide.old: In this book the treble staff is Queensland, the Queen's land. Start on its top line, F. Just above it, in the space, is G. Then ladder 1 carries A, the next space B, and ladder 2 carries C: high C. One letter a step, just like inside the staff, up to ladder 3: E.
guide.new: In this book the treble staff is Queensland, the Queen's land. Start on its top line, F. The space above is G. Ladder 1 is A, the next space B, and ladder 2 is C, high C. One letter a step, up to ladder 3: E.

guide.old: The bass staff is Kingsland, the King's land. Climb down from its bottom line, G. Just under it is F. Ladder 1 carries E, the next space D, and ladder 2 carries C: low C. One letter a step, backwards (G F E D C), down to ladder 3: A.
guide.new: The bass staff is Kingsland, the King's land. Climb down from its bottom line, G. The space below is F. Ladder 1 is E, the next space D, and ladder 2 is C, low C. One letter a step, backwards, down to ladder 3: A.

guide.old: Middle C sits on one ladder, seen from either staff. The same key can be written two ways, so each hand can stay in its own staff.
guide.new: Middle C sits on one ladder, seen from either staff. The same key, written two ways, lets each hand stay in its own staff.

guide.old: From low to high there are five Cs, an octave apart: low C on two ladders under the bass staff, bass C in the bass staff's second space, middle C on its ladder, treble C in the treble staff's third space, and high C on two ladders over the treble staff.
guide.new: Five Cs sit an octave apart: low C two ladders under the bass staff, bass C in its second space, middle C on its ladder, treble C in the treble staff's third space, and high C two ladders over the treble staff.

guide.old: Fold the grand staff in half at middle C, as in the chapter before, and the Cs meet in pairs: treble C on bass C. And now high C on low C, two ledger lines up, two ledger lines down.
guide.new: Fold the grand staff at middle C, as in the chapter before, and the Cs meet in pairs: treble C on bass C, now high C on low C, two ledger lines up, two down.

guide.old: Neat or not: circle a tick or a cross for four notes, then draw the ledger lines seven notes need on dotted guide lines (some need none). Then count how many each of seven notes on a big staff needs: 0, 1, 2 or 3. One A4 page.
guide.new: Neat or not: circle a tick or a cross for four notes. Draw the ledger lines seven notes need on dotted guide lines. Some need none. Count how many each of seven notes on a big staff needs: 0, 1, 2 or 3. One A4 page.

guide.old: A short line drawn above or below the staff for one note that is too high or too low for the five lines. The line-space pattern carries on through ledger lines exactly as it does inside the staff. "Leger line" is another spelling of the same thing.
guide.new: A short line above or below the staff, for one note too high or too low for the five lines. The line-space pattern carries on through it, as inside the staff. Its other spelling is "leger line".

guide.old: First count out from the edge of the staff (line, space, ledger line), one letter a step. Then learn a few ledger notes by heart, such as high C, two ledger lines above the treble staff, and low C, two ledger lines below the bass staff. Read the notes near them as a step or a skip away.
guide.new: First count out from the staff, one letter a step: line, space, ledger line. Then learn a few ledger notes by heart, such as high C, two ledger lines above the treble staff, and low C, two below the bass staff. Read the notes near them as a step or a skip away.

guide.old: Draw it a little wider than the note head, the same distance apart as the staff lines, with no gaps back to the staff. Draw only as many as the note needs: a note just above or below the staff needs none, and a note in a space gets no extra line on top, like a lid.
guide.new: Draw it a little wider than the note head, the same distance apart as the staff lines, with no gaps back to the staff. Only as many as the note needs: a note just above or below the staff needs none, and a note in a space gets no lid on top.

guide.old: Between the treble and bass staves, a note can be written with ledger lines under the treble staff or on the bass staff (or with ledger lines over the bass staff). It is the same key on the piano. Writing it in the hand's own staff keeps each hand in one place on the page.
guide.new: Between the staves, a note can sit on ledger lines under the treble staff, on the bass staff, or on ledger lines over the bass staff. It is the same key on the piano. Writing it in each hand's own staff keeps the hands in place on the page.
